rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Quraysh, Noah’s people and later nations such as ʿĀd and Thamūd denied their messengers, tried to seize them, and used frivolous falsehood against the truth.
rows.anchor: each nation wanted to lay their hands on its messenger and tried to defeat his cause through their frivolous talk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment follows naturally from rebellious deeds, so it is neither injustice nor oppression; their fate is a lesson, not grounds for sympathy.
rows.anchor: a natural consequence of their deeds; it is certainly no injustice or oppression to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah was revealed while Quraysh leaders were consulting about seizing the Prophet, and the warning assures him and his companions.
rows.anchor: when the leaders of the Quraysh were consulting one another to lay their hands on the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fulfilled decision refers to God’s response to Satan: those who leave God’s path to follow Satan will be gathered in Hell.
rows.anchor: those who while leaving the path of God follow Satan shall all be gathered in Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the decision came true for earlier nations, it has come true for Quraysh; the Prophet must discharge his duty while they meet their ordained fate.
rows.anchor: just as this decision of God was fulfilled for the previous nations, it has also been fulfilled for these disbelievers of the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is called Hell because it is the first step toward Hell.
rows.anchor: Since the punishment of God is the first step to Hell, hence this punishment is signified by the word Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the favored throne-bearing angels fear God while praising Him; people who rely on angelic recommendations should consider how much more the rest of creation must fear Him.
rows.anchor: continue to remain fearful and afraid of Him and remain busy in extolling Him and celebrating His praises

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ belief shows they claim no divinity; like God’s servants, they profess faith in Him.
rows.anchor: like the servants of God, they profess faith in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels seek forgiveness for believers as an intercession reserved for those who believe in God.
rows.anchor: This seeking of forgiveness by them is their recommendation and is reserved for the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to shield the believers from punishment in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: shield them from the punishment of this world and the next.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ fear and plea for earth’s inhabitants also appear in the previous sūrah’s last verse and in 42:5.
rows.anchor: can be seen in the last verse of the previous sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly imagine their favored angels will prevent God from punishing their worshippers, but the angels remain submissive and fear His wrath.
rows.anchor: they will not allow their worshippers to be seized by God come what may.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels defer every matter to God’s encompassing mercy and knowledge rather than speaking as though they had authority over His decisions.
rows.anchor: they do not speak to their Lord as if they have some say in matters under His jurisdiction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer is for people who repent, reform themselves, and then follow God’s path.
rows.anchor: people who repent from their sins and after reforming themselves follow the path of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ advocacy does not extend to enemies of the Messenger and his religion.
rows.anchor: This is not for those who are the enemies of the Messenger and his religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask Paradise for believers’ forebears, wives, and progeny only when each has become worthy through repentance and reform; kinship alone does not earn Paradise.
rows.anchor: these angels pray for only those among the forefathers, wives and progeny of the believers who become worthy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “Mighty, Wise” expresses intercession and is also spoken by Jesus in 5:120.
rows.anchor: an expression of intercession which is also cited through the tongue of Jesus (sws) in verse 120

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer entrusts the matter to God’s power, while His wisdom means He acts only with wisdom and justice.
rows.anchor: He can do whatever He wants to; however, since God is also wise, He will only do that which is based on His wisdom and justice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sins” refers to their consequences; a verb can name the outcome of an action.
rows.anchor: To convey the outcome of an action, at times, a verb is used to connote its consequence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels see the Day of Accountability as dreadful and regard being protected from sin’s consequences as the real success.
rows.anchor: To them, the real fortunate are people whom the Almighty protected from the consequences of their sins

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ intercession has the limited form described in the Qur’an; those reminded of reality respond with debate and confrontation rather than relying on it to escape the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: when they are reminded of the actual reality they are impelled to debate and confrontation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s former aversion to the rejecters was greater than their later grief over their own loss and leaders’ errors, because they arrogantly rejected the messengers’ call.
rows.anchor: much more than the sorrow and anger they will have at that time on their misfortune and deprivation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment follows after truth was conclusively conveyed, and no one remains to help them.
rows.anchor: Whatever has come before them has come after the truth has been conclusively conveyed to them from the Almighty; they deserve only this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “faith” specifically means tawḥīd, the only form of faith acceptable to God.
rows.anchor: Faith here specially refers to faith in tawḥīd. This is because only that faith is acceptable to God which exists with tawḥīd.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters’ greatest aversion is the call to tawḥīd, as 39:45 says; 40:12 likewise explains their anger by their rejection of tawḥīd and preference for shirk.
rows.anchor: the greatest aversion which the rejecters have is for the call of tawḥīd.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters admit they thought resurrection impossible and mocked the Messenger; after witnessing life after death, they ask whether they can leave Hell and return to live faithfully.
rows.anchor: They would say that they did think that raising the dead back to life was something impossible

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two lives are earthly life and the life of the next world.
rows.anchor: life of the next world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fate follows stubborn rejection of tawḥīd and ardent support for shirk; judgment now rests with God, and the judgment is the fate they face.
rows.anchor: so now the decision rests with the Almighty and this decision is nothing but what they are now facing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both mercy and calamity are in God’s hands; thunder, lightning, and rain show that one God controls the heavens and earth and holds punishment and provision.
rows.anchor: This is a clear proof of the fact that both the heavens and the earth are in the control of one God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs and provision instruct people, but only the attentive and discerning benefit; desire-blinded people cannot be opened by even great signs.
rows.anchor: benefiting from them depends on the fact that a person is inclined to observe them and also has a discerning mind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims are told to call on God alone with pure obedience even if the disbelievers dislike it.
rows.anchor: Muslims should only call upon God without associating anyone with Him and worship Him with purity of obedience.
